raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ### What does this PR do? Makes vLLM's ModelOpt MXFP8 config **exclude only the modules it names**, for configs that verl generates and marks. Today the router exclusion `model.layers.N.mlp.gate` also excludes the dense `model.layers.N.mlp.gate_up_proj`, so MXFP8 rollout serves `gate_proj` and `up_proj` in BF16 while training runs them in MXFP8. On `main` nothing marks a config yet, so behavior there is unchanged. This is part 3 of the split of #7519 (end-to-end MXFP8 RL on Blackwell). It depends only on main; #8129 (MXFP8 vLLM rollout) is stacked on it and marks the configs it generates. | # | PR | Depends on | |---|---|---| | 1 | #8127: MXFP8 training + shared TE quantizer | main | | 2 | #8128: quantized-rollout sentinel | main | | 3 | **this PR**: exact MXFP8 exclusion matcher | main | | 4 | #8129: MXFP8 vLLM rollout | 1, 3 | | 5 | #8130: MXFP8 SGLang rollout + refit loader | 1 | | 6 | #8131: post-sync refit self-check | 4, 5 | | 7 | #8132: quantized-layer audit | 6 | **Why.** - verl keeps MoE routers in high precision by putting `model.layers.N.mlp.gate` for every decoder layer into `ignored_layers`, dense models included. - vLLM's FP8 config matches these names exactly, so FP8 rollout on `main` is not affected. - MXFP8 rollout (#8129) goes through `ModelOptMxFp8Config`. Its `is_layer_excluded` (vLLM 0.24, unchanged in 0.29) falls back to substring matching, `exclude_module in prefix`, which vLLM keeps for checkpoints exported by ModelOpt < 0.39. `model.layers.N.mlp.gate` is a substring of `model.layers.N.mlp.gate_up_proj`, so the fused projection is built unquantized. - On Qwen3-1.7B that is 56 of 311 synced parameters: `gate_proj` and `up_proj` in all 28 layers. Nothing in the metrics shows it: train–rollout KL stayed at 0.007–0.010, inside the healthy range. Only asking the engine for its parameter dtypes exposed it (#8132). **What.** - **Opt-in marker.** verl adds `_verl_exact_mxfp8_exclusions: true` to the MXFP8 quantization config it generates. A wrapper on `ModelOptMxFp8Config.from_config` copies it onto the parsed config as a plain boolean, which survives serialization to the workers. - **Strict matching, marked configs only.** The `is_layer_excluded` wrapper matches module names exactly, plus explicit `fnmatch` globs, against the fused name and its HF shards. It then passes the matches to vLLM's own `is_layer_skipped`, so the all-or-none check for fused layers still applies. Unmarked configs (checkpoints, other formats) call the original matcher. - **Fails closed.** A marked config that is not `quant_method: mxfp8`, is not a `ModelOptMxFp8Config`, or has malformed `exclude_modules` / `packed_modules_mapping` raises instead of silently keeping the substring rule. - **Installation.** `build_fp8_method_patchers` returns the two wrappers with the existing FP8 refit patchers (vLLM ≥ 0.20), so they are installed wherever verl installs those: in the server before vLLM parses the config, and in each worker. The module is imported only when vLLM has `ModelOptMxFp8Config`. Otherwise CPU tests that load `vllm_fp8_utils.py` against a stubbed vLLM break: main's `test_vllm_fp8_restage_same_shape_on_cpu.py` failed 3 of 3. **Evidence on B200** (#7519): - **Qwen3-1.7B**, vLLM 0.24, MXFP8 rollout from #8129, 2 training steps: - without the matcher, the quantized-layer audit's engine re-check (#8132) reported 56 disagreements: `mlp.gate_proj` and `mlp.up_proj` in all 28 layers; - with it, 0 of 311 parameters disagree, and the weight sync loads the fused MXFP8 `gate_up_proj` without a shape mismatch. - **What leaving gate/up in BF16 costs.** In one engine at fixed weights (Qwen3-8B, learning rate 0, paired prompts), train–rollout KL with an MXFP8 learner falls, against a BF16 sampler: - 10.6% [8.6, 12.7] when `gate_up_proj` stays in BF16, the state this bug produces; - 16.1% [14.1, 18.1] when every linear is MXFP8. ### Checklist Before Starting - [x] Search for similar PRs: https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+is_layer_excluded. No other open PR changes the ModelOpt exclusion matching; this is part 3 of #7519's split. - [x] PR title formatted as `[rollout] fix: ...` ### Test ```bash python -m pytest tests/utils/test_mxfp8_exclusion_patch_on_cpu.py -q # 30 passed python -m pytest tests/utils/test_mxfp8_exclusion_patch_on_cpu.py tests/utils/test_vllm_quant_utils_moe_on_cpu.py -q # 34 passed # on current main + this PR; the test calls build_fp8_method_patchers against a stubbed vLLM: python -m pytest tests/utils/test_vllm_fp8_restage_same_shape_on_cpu.py -q # 3 passed (3 failed before the import fix) ``` `pre-commit run` passes on all changed files. ### API and Usage Example No user-facing change. A caller that generates an MXFP8 config opts in by marking it; #8129 does this in `vLLMHttpServer._apply_quantization`: ```python from verl.utils.vllm.mxfp8_exclusion_patch import VERL_EXACT_MXFP8_EXCLUSIONS hf_overrides["quantization_config"] = { "quant_method": "mxfp8", "ignored_layers": all_mlp_gate_layers + ["lm_head", "model.embed_tokens"], VERL_EXACT_MXFP8_EXCLUSIONS: True, } ``` Do not mark user or checkpoint configs. ### Design & Code Changes - `verl/utils/vllm/mxfp8_exclusion_patch.py`: the marker, the strict matcher, the fail-closed checks, and `build_mxfp8_exclusion_patchers()` (two unstarted patches on `ModelOptMxFp8Config`; none on vLLM without ModelOpt MXFP8). - `verl/utils/vllm/vllm_fp8_utils.py`: `build_fp8_method_patchers` appends them on vLLM ≥ 0.20, importing the module only when `ModelOptMxFp8Config` exists. - `verl/utils/vllm/vllm_quant_utils.py`: docstring only: install before the config is parsed and in every model-building worker. - `docs/low_precision/mxfp8_exclusion_patch.md`: the bug, the opt-in contract and the matching rules. - `tests/utils/test_mxfp8_exclusion_patch_on_cpu.py`: - the 28-layer dense case (routers excluded, `gate_up_proj` quantized); - instance isolation, and unmarked checkpoint configs unchanged; - fused shards and globs, and no implicit parent or suffix matching; - the marker surviving parsing and pickling; - fail-closed inputs; - restoring the class when the patches stop; - the registry with and without ModelOpt MXFP8. ### AI assistance disclosure Developed with AI assistance. @@ -0,0 +1,106 @@
+# Opt-in MXFP8 exclusion patch
+
+Last updated: 10/13/2026
+
+## Status and scope
+
+The parser/matcher patches are registered in `build_fp8_method_patchers()` and
+installed through the existing `apply_vllm_quant_patches()` lifecycle. This does
+not add CUDA MXFP8 rollout support to `main`: the MXFP8 feature branch must still
+mark its generated configs explicitly. Without that marker behavior is unchanged.
+
+vLLM's `ModelOptQuantConfigBase.is_layer_excluded()` (0.24 to 0.29) includes a legacy
+substring fallback. A router exclusion such as `model.layers.0.mlp.gate` also
+matches the dense SwiGLU `model.layers.0.mlp.gate_up_proj`. Both HF projections
+(`gate_proj` and `up_proj`) can consequently remain unquantized in rollout.
+The upstream comment about ModelOpt 0.39 is not a runtime version guard.
+
+`build_mxfp8_exclusion_patchers()` supplies two wrappers on the
+`ModelOptMxFp8Config` subclass: `from_config()` transfers the explicit opt-in to
+the parsed instance; `is_layer_excluded()` uses strict matching only when that
+instance is marked. Unmarked configs call the original matcher. The ModelOpt
+base class, other quantization classes, and `get_quant_method()` are untouched.
+
+## Integration contract for the MXFP8 feature branch
+
+1. Only when verl itself generates an online MXFP8 HF quantization config, add
+   `_verl_exact_mxfp8_exclusions: true`. Do not add this marker to loaded user or
+   checkpoint configs. Keep all real router/high-precision exclusions; this helper
+   fixes matching, not router discovery across model architectures.
+2. Install the common patches BEFORE vLLM parses that raw HF config. The parser
+   wrapper explicitly saves the boolean marker; upstream normalization need not
+   preserve unknown dictionary fields. Patching only after parsing loses provenance.
+3. In **each model-building worker**, install the common patches before creating
+   linear/MoE layers. Parsed configs carry only a boolean marker across serialization,
+   not instance-bound methods. Existing worker startup installs the common patches;
+   feature-branch integration must verify this also holds on its MXFP8 paths.
+   A driver-only patch or a post-refit call is insufficient.
+
+```python
+from verl.utils.vllm.mxfp8_exclusion_patch import VERL_EXACT_MXFP8_EXCLUSIONS
+from verl.utils.vllm.vllm_quant_utils import apply_vllm_quant_patches
+
+# Future integration: ONLY the config generated by verl for online MXFP8.
+hf_quant_config = {
+    "quant_method": "mxfp8",
+    "ignored_layers": ["model.layers.0.mlp.gate", "lm_head", "model.embed_tokens"],
+    VERL_EXACT_MXFP8_EXCLUSIONS: True,
+}
+
+# In the launcher, BEFORE creating/parsing the vLLM config:
+apply_vllm_quant_patches()

+## Matching contract
+
+- An ordinary entry matches a module when it equals a run of whole dot-separated
+  components of the module's name: `lm_head` matches `lm_head` and
+  `language_model.lm_head`, `model.layers.0.mlp` matches its descendants such as

+  this is not a new per-expert precision policy.

+    """Model vLLM's exact-match helper, including fusion and expert-group handling."""
+    leaf = prefix.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
+    if leaf in fused_mapping:
+        if prefix in ignored_layers:
+            return True
+        parent, separator, _ = prefix.rpartition(".")

+"""Opt-in exclusion matching for verl-generated ModelOpt MXFP8 configs.
+
+vLLM's ModelOpt matcher (0.24 to 0.29) retains a legacy substring fallback. A generated
+router exclusion ``mlp.gate`` consequently excludes the SwiGLU ``mlp.gate_up_proj``
+too. On an explicitly opted-in config instance this helper matches at module-name
+component boundaries instead: an entry excludes a module when it equals a run of
+whole dot-separated components of the module's name (``lm_head`` still excludes
+``language_model.lm_head``), so only matches that cut through a component, like
+``gate`` inside ``gate_up_proj``, are dropped. Checkpoint configs and other
+quantization methods retain their behavior.
+
+The patchers are registered by ``build_fp8_method_patchers``. The MXFP8 feature
+branch must still mark its generated configs explicitly. See
+``docs/low_precision/mxfp8_exclusion_patch.md`` for the integration contract.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Mapping
+from fnmatch import fnmatchcase
+from functools import wraps
+from typing import Any
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+# Keep provenance in the HF config passed between processes, not a global env var.
+VERL_EXACT_MXFP8_EXCLUSIONS = "_verl_exact_mxfp8_exclusions"
+
+
+def _matches(name: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
+    """``pattern`` is a run of whole dot-separated components of ``name``, or an fnmatch glob matching it."""
+    return f".{pattern}." in f".{name}." or fnmatchcase(name, pattern)
+
+
+def _is_layer_excluded(self, prefix: str) -> bool:
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.quant_utils import is_layer_skipped
+
+    excluded = self.exclude_modules
+    mapping = self.packed_modules_mapping
+    if not excluded:
+        return False
+
+    # Resolve component-run and glob matches against both the engine's fused name
+    # and its HF shards. Feed literal matches into vLLM's helper so its all-or-none

> vLLM 0.24's ModelOptQuantConfigBase.is_layer_excluded() keeps a legacy substring fallback (exclude_module in prefix), so model.layers.N.mlp.gate also matches the dense SwiGLU model.layers.N.mlp.gate_up_proj.
